name: Bathroom disrepair
title: Bathroom Disrepair Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: When bathroom disrepair affects everyday life
intro: Broken fittings, persistent leaks and unusable washing or toilet facilities can seriously disrupt a household. If your landlord knew about the problem and failed to complete an effective repair, legal options may be available.
compensation: An assessment may consider how long essential bathroom facilities were restricted, whether water damage affected other rooms, damage to belongings and reasonable additional costs caused by the defect.
evidence: Photographs of leaks, broken fittings and damaged surfaces
Repair reports and contractor attendance records
A timeline of periods when facilities could not be used
Receipts for cleaning, alternative facilities or damaged items

name: Boiler and heating
title: Boiler and Heating Disrepair Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Claims involving broken boilers and unreliable heating
intro: Repeated boiler failures or extended periods without heating or hot water can make a rented home difficult to use, particularly in winter or where vulnerable people live in the property.
compensation: Relevant factors can include the duration and season of the failure, loss of heating or hot water, reasonable electricity costs for temporary heaters and any supported effect on health.
evidence: Boiler fault codes and repair records
Dates of every loss of heating or hot water
Energy bills and receipts for temporary heaters
Medical evidence where cold conditions affected health

name: Crumbling plaster
title: Crumbling Plaster Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Loose or falling plaster should be properly investigated
intro: Crumbling plaster may be caused by water ingress, persistent damp or movement. Repeatedly covering the surface may not resolve the underlying defect or the safety risk.
compensation: A claim assessment may consider loss of use of affected rooms, damage to furniture or flooring, cleaning costs and any injury caused by falling material, where supported by evidence.
evidence: Dated photographs showing deterioration
Reports of falling or loose material
Records of earlier patch repairs
Receipts and photographs of damaged belongings

name: Damp and mould
title: Damp and Mould Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Persistent damp and mould should not become normal
intro: Where mould keeps returning, the cause may involve leaks, the building fabric, heating, insulation or ventilation. A landlord should investigate reported conditions and address defects for which it is responsible.
compensation: The assessment may reflect affected rooms, duration, damaged clothing or furniture, additional heating or cleaning costs and medically evidenced effects on physical or mental health.
evidence: Dated photographs from each affected room
A timeline of reports and recurring mould
Receipts for damaged possessions or extra heating
Medical records where health was affected

name: Defective brickwork
title: Defective Brickwork Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Damaged brickwork can affect safety and weatherproofing
intro: Cracked, loose or deteriorating brickwork can allow water into the home or create a safety concern. The cause and seriousness should be properly assessed.
compensation: Relevant losses may include disruption from water penetration, restricted use of affected areas, damaged belongings and reasonable expenses caused by the unresolved defect.
evidence: Clear photographs of cracks or loose masonry
Reports showing water entering near the defect
Survey, contractor or building-control records
A record of earlier repairs and recurrence

name: Dangerous wiring
title: Dangerous Wiring Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
intro: Exposed wiring, overheating sockets, burning smells or water near electrical fittings can create an immediate hazard. Avoid the affected area and use the landlord’s emergency reporting route.
compensation: An assessment may consider periods without safe electricity, loss of essential facilities, damaged appliances, temporary accommodation costs and any proven injury or financial loss.
evidence: Safe photographs of visible defects
Emergency repair reference numbers
Electrician or contractor findings
Evidence of outages, damaged appliances or other loss

name: Roofs and gutters
title: Roof and Gutter Disrepair Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Recurring water ingress needs an effective repair
intro: Defective roofs and gutters can cause penetrating damp, damaged ceilings and repeated internal leaks. Temporary patching may not be enough where the source remains unresolved.
compensation: The impact may include unusable rooms, damaged decoration or belongings, cleaning and drying costs and the length of time water continued to enter after notice.
evidence: Photos or videos during and after rainfall
Repair references and roofing inspection records
Images of internal water damage
Receipts for damaged items, cleaning or drying equipment

name: Defective sanitaryware
title: Defective Sanitaryware Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Essential sanitary facilities should remain safe and usable
intro: Broken toilets, basins, baths and related pipework can cause leaks, hygiene concerns and loss of essential facilities when repairs are delayed or ineffective.
compensation: The assessment may consider how essential facilities were affected, the duration of the problem, water damage and reasonable costs incurred because sanitaryware could not be safely used.
evidence: Photographs of broken or leaking fittings
Dates facilities were unusable
Repair and plumbing records
Receipts for reasonable additional expenses

name: Spray foam insulation
title: Spray Foam Insulation Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Defective insulation should be assessed carefully
intro: Poorly installed or inappropriate spray foam can contribute to moisture, ventilation or roof-timber concerns. Responsibility depends on who arranged the work and the evidence about the resulting condition.
compensation: Any claim would be assessed on proven property impact, loss of use, reasonable investigation or remedial costs and other losses legally connected to the defective work.
evidence: Installation documents and guarantees
Surveyor or roofing reports
Photographs of condensation or affected timbers
Correspondence identifying who arranged the work

name: Electrical faults
title: Electrical Fault Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Repeated electrical faults should not be ignored
intro: Frequent outages, faulty sockets and unsafe landlord-supplied installations can disrupt daily life and may create serious risks requiring prompt investigation.
compensation: Relevant considerations may include loss of power, inability to use rooms or appliances, damaged electrical items, reasonable alternative costs and any supported injury.
evidence: Fault and outage dates
Electrician or contractor reports
Repair references and complaint responses
Receipts or proof of damaged appliances

name: Faulty gas appliances
title: Faulty Gas Appliance Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Faulty gas appliances must be treated seriously
intro: A landlord-supplied boiler, fire or cooker that is unsafe or repeatedly breaks down may require urgent action. Follow safety advice and report suspected gas danger immediately.
compensation: An assessment may consider loss of heating, hot water or cooking facilities, reasonable temporary costs and any medically supported harm, subject to responsibility and evidence.
evidence: Gas safety and engineer records
Warning notices or appliance fault details
Dates essential facilities were unavailable
Receipts for reasonable temporary alternatives

name: Flooding and water damage
title: Flooding and Water Damage Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Flooding can affect far more than decoration
intro: Water entering through roofs, pipes, drains or communal systems can damage belongings, make rooms unusable and create electrical, damp and mould hazards.
compensation: Possible heads of loss include reduced use of the home, damaged possessions, cleaning and drying costs, temporary accommodation and supported health effects.
evidence: Videos and photographs during the incident
Evidence identifying the source of water
An inventory of damaged belongings
Receipts for cleaning, drying or accommodation

name: Insect infestation
title: Insect Infestation Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Recurring insect infestations may be linked to disrepair
intro: Cockroaches, bedbugs or other insects may enter or persist because of structural gaps, drainage, communal conditions or defects controlled by the landlord.
compensation: The impact assessment may include contaminated belongings, treatment and cleaning costs, loss of use and distress or health effects where these are properly evidenced.
evidence: Photographs and pest-control reports
Evidence of structural entry points
Treatment dates and recurrence records
Receipts for cleaning or damaged belongings

name: Kitchen disrepair
title: Kitchen Disrepair Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: A damaged kitchen can make a home difficult to use
intro: Leaks, unsafe units, broken worktops and defective landlord-controlled plumbing can affect food preparation, hygiene and the safe use of the room.
compensation: Relevant factors may include loss of cooking or washing facilities, water damage, reasonable additional food costs and how long the kitchen remained partly or wholly unusable.
evidence: Photographs of damaged units and fittings
Dates facilities could not be used
Plumbing and repair records
Receipts for reasonable additional costs

name: Plumbing and active leaks
title: Plumbing and Drainage Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Recurring leaks and drainage failures need a lasting solution
intro: Leaking pipes, blocked landlord-controlled drains and repeated wastewater problems can cause property damage, hygiene risks and loss of essential facilities.
compensation: An assessment may include loss of use, damage to possessions, cleaning costs, additional water or utility charges and the effect of prolonged sanitation problems.
evidence: Photos and videos of each incident
Plumber, drainage or contractor reports
Water bills where consumption increased
Receipts for damage, cleaning and other expenses

name: Unsafe flooring
title: Unsafe Flooring Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Loose or collapsing floors can create a serious risk
intro: Rotten boards, unstable surfaces and persistent trip hazards should be assessed, particularly where leaks or structural defects have weakened the floor.
compensation: A claim may consider restricted use of rooms, relocation or alternative accommodation costs, damaged possessions and proven injury caused by the defect.
evidence: Photographs showing movement or damage
Reports of falls or near misses
Surveyor and contractor findings
Records showing rooms could not be safely used

name: Vermin and pest infestation
title: Vermin and Pest Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Structural defects can allow vermin into a home
intro: Rats and mice may enter through broken air bricks, gaps, drains or communal areas. Treatment alone may fail unless the landlord repairs the route of entry.
compensation: Relevant losses may include contaminated food or belongings, cleaning and treatment costs, unusable areas and evidenced health or wellbeing impacts.
evidence: Photographs of vermin and entry points
Pest-control reports identifying the source
Communal-area and drainage reports
Receipts for treatment, cleaning and damaged items

name: Windows and doors
title: Window and Door Disrepair Claims | Housing Condition Claims UK
h1: Windows and external doors should be secure and weatherproof
intro: Broken locks, failed frames, severe draughts and water penetration can affect security, warmth and the safe use of a rented home.
compensation: An assessment may consider heat loss and additional energy costs, water damage, security-related disruption, loss of use and the duration of the unresolved problem.
evidence: Photographs of gaps, damage or water ingress
Repair reports and appointment history
Energy bills showing additional heating costs
Police or incident records where security was affected
